newsitem.title: CROATIA: World Bank signs 160 mln mark loan for Croatia.
newsitem.headline: World Bank signs 160 mln mark loan for Croatia.

text.p: Croatia and the World Bank have signed an agreement on a 160 million German mark loan aimed at overhauling Croatia's banking system and restructuring its large utilities, Croatian officials said on Thursday.

"This is the Enterprise and Financial Sector Adjustment Loan (EFSAL)...It is a support to reforms in the banking system and to help further overhauling of banks," said Hrvoje Radovanic, assistant to Croatian Foreign Minister Bozo Prka.
He said the loan, which was signed in Washington on Wednesday, would also be used to restructure large public sector firms.

The EFSAL loan shows "the confidence the World Bank has in the transitional success of the Croatian economy," daily Vjesnik quoted the bank's regional vice-president for Europe and Central Asia Hans Apitz as saying.
He said the loan was the first of its kind the World Bank had approved for Croatia.
The World Bank is also planning to open a Croatian office in late summer and has appointed a director for Croatia who will taker over her duties on July 1, Vjesnik said.

Croatian officials earlier said the laon would be used to restructure troubled Privredna Banka and to help the continued rehabilitation of Splitska and Rijecka banks, both of which have already been recapitalised.
The loan will also be used to help ailing state firms such as Croatian railways, HPT telecom and others.

The Croatian government decided last year to overhaul 16 trouble state-owned firms by shifting ther debts to state banks and utilities, or covering them from the Privatisation Fund portfolio. It said it would need some $250 million to revive them. -- Zagreb newsroom + 385 1 455 7075
